items.title: Inference Optimization with CoreWeave Mission Control Agent
items.summary: CoreWeave Mission Control Agent, built into the CoreWeave Console, helps teams get more useful work from the GPUs they already have. In this demo, we show how it traces a slow CoreWeave Dedicated Inference endpoint serving agentic traffic to KV cache pressure, then quantizes the model to NVFP4 and reshapes it from one replica to two on the same eight GB200 GPUs. Load tests verify each change, showing more than 3x the output throughput per GPU with no new hardware. ⏳Timestamps: 0:09 Introducing CoreWeave Mission Control Agent 0:25 A healthy endpoint that has outgrown its configuration 1:16 Asking Mission Control Agent to investigate 2:19 Root cause: KV cache pressure under agentic traffic 3:03 Quantizing the model to NVFP4 on the same GPUs 4:09 Reshaping to two replicas at TP4 5:20 Load test results and applying TP4 7:37 More than 3x output per GPU on the same hardware

items.title: Using AI Won't Save Your Job
items.summary: Everyone says learn AI and you'll be safe. I think that skips the part where your company decides what to do with all your new speed. I keep hearing that people who use AI will win and everyone else will lose. Getting faster could help you take on better work and earn more, or it could mean your company keeps fewer people around. Both are possible. So I'd want people who trust my work, skills another employer would pay for, and maybe customers of my own. None of that is a guarantee. If your company didn't need you tomorrow, where could you take what you know?

items.title: How Indian Banks Can Stop Digital Fraud Without Hurting User Experience
items.summary: Digital fraud in India is running at 7.1%, nearly double the global average, as fraudsters move from hacking networks to synthetic identities, credit washing and account takeover. This conversation looks at how banks and lenders can use alternative data to stop digital fraud without hurting the user experience. items.title: Connection Isn’t Cognition: Why AI Agents Can’t Think Together (with Vijoy Pandey)
items.summary: In Episode #1041, Dr. Vijoy Pandey (SVP and General Manager of Outshift, Cisco's incubation engine) returns for a third visit to explain why multi-agent systems fail without anyone noticing. Agents from different vendors, clouds and organisations can now exchange perfectly valid messages, but connection is not cognition: they do not agree on what those messages mean. Vijoy's team analyzed multi-agent sessions from its own production deployments and from public traces, and found a cognitive failure in every single one. In this episode, he lays out the kinds of failure he sees and how fast they compound, introduces the open-source observability platform and protocols Outshift has shipped to catch and correct drift mid-task, details a record-breaking quantum network running on real New York City fiber, and explains why probabilistic AI software running on deterministic hardware is a mismatch worth fixing. items.summary: Joscha Bach on a dream he had when he was two or three. He was about to eat a chocolate with a very strong smell, and he woke up just before it reached his mouth. items.title: Simulated Water Can't Make You Wet (Joscha Bach)
items.summary: Joscha Bach on a joke that turned out to be true. In Minecraft, if you're on fire and jump into water, the fire goes out because you're wet. Someone then trained a neural network on nothing but Minecraft's visuals, so you could play a simulated Minecraft with no game code underneath. Joscha set out to joke that simulated water in simulated Minecraft can't make you wet. He tried it, and it was literally true: the water receded as you walked in, because the network had never learned what it means to be immersed. #Shorts Watch the full conversation: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yW_ngvMFlYs

items.title: New-Grad Unemployment Didn't Spike This Summer
items.summary: New-grad unemployment didn’t spike this summer, but that’s only half the story. A new NBER working paper gives the first estimates of AI’s effect on new-grad unemployment for summer 2026, and the headline finding is that unemployment held steady. The other half comes from a Census Bureau working paper that looked at pay. Starting earnings fell about 13% for grads in the most AI-exposed majors. The unemployment rate shows whether you have a job. It doesn’t show what the job pays. So new grads can still be getting hired while their first paychecks are getting smaller.
